about: Springbrook Hollow Farm Distillery sits in the foothills of the Adirondacks, about five miles from Lake George, on land Dave Bannon long kept as a horse farm. He and a group of old school friends, Matt Colucci, Mike Forcier, Tony DeSantis and Ken Rohne, began distilling in his antique barn and opened to the public in December 2014. The name comes from the spring that feeds the farm, drawn from a 600-foot well, and the team uses that water, unstripped, in every bottle.

This is Springbrook’s Adirondack Blended Straight Bourbon. Rather than bottle only what their own still has produced, the distillers marry Springbrook’s house straight bourbon with straight bourbons of different ages and mash bills sourced from across the country, adjusting the blend until it reaches the balance they want. Every component is a straight bourbon, aged at least two years in new charred oak, and the finished whiskey is brought down with the farm’s Adirondack spring water to 43% alcohol.

The distillery describes the result simply as a smooth, full-bodied whiskey. Growth followed the bottles: Springbrook moved from the barn into a new 8,000-square-foot, Adirondack-style distillery and tasting room on Route 149, and its spirits now travel to farmers’ markets and shops well beyond Lake George, while the old barn on Clements Road still anchors the family farm where it all began.
